To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reaction of ammonia with acetonitrile in a flow system in the presence of a zeolite catalyst results in the production of formamide, and that formamide can be converted to acetic acid in the presence of zeolite.

the reaction of formamide with acetonitrile in the presence of Al2O3 at 300 C leads to a crystalline compound C12H23N5O2, which was identified as N-(α-Aminoisobutyryl)‐N’-(2‐imino‐3,5,5‐trimethyl‐3‐pyrrolidinyl)‐formamide.
the reaction of formamide with acetonitrile in the presence of Al2O3 at 300 °C leads to the formation of a new compound C12H23N5O2.

the formamid‐aceton reaction at 300 °C over Al _{2} O _{3} leads to a crystalline compound C _{12} H _{23} O _{2} N _{5} in good yield.

the formamide‐aceton reaction is not a reaction of the formamid radical with aceton, but a reaction of aceton with the formamide radical.
